title: tiered-provisioning-gating-and-transient-credit-controller
author: Anika Rao
description: Introduce a tiered provisioning gate and a transient credit controller to allow safe short-lived burst access to opportunistic capacity while preserving long-term throughput guarantees for reserved tenants. Motivation: customers using Dedicated capacity wanted predictable committed throughput but also asked for controlled microbursts (for traffic spikes) without permanently increasing reservation size. This change implements a gating layer that separates 'committed' and 'opportunistic' provisioning paths, a lightweight transient-credit allocator with configurable half-life and max-burst budgets, and signal-driven admission heuristics that integrate with the existing reservation and warm-pool managers. Key behaviors: 1) committed requests always get priority and bypass opportunistic gating; 2) opportunistic requests can be granted transient credits up to tenant-specific burst budgets; 3) credits decay over time and are replenished slowly to avoid supply exhaustion; 4) under sustained saturation, the gate rejects opportunistic requests and falls back to queueing or soft-throttling per route policy; 5) telemetry emits per-tenant credit issuance, decay, reject-rates, and credit-lifetime histograms. Implementation notes: added a Gate interface and implementations for TieredGate and NoopGate (for older clusters), a TransientCreditController that is eventually-consistent and runs compact in the provisioner loop, and cross-checked safety for reservation leakage (credits are scoped to request contexts and reconciled on pod eviction). The PR also adds an opt-in feature flag (dedicated.tieredProvisioning.enabled) and a canary rollout plan (10% of pools for 24h) described in the ops doc. Includes unit and integration tests plus a small upgrade path adapter to migrate clusters that use warm-pool overrides. CI: unit + integration + e2e route smoke (flaky e2e re-run once). Merge method: squash and merge. Related: ENG-2134, SUP-9021.

review_comments: Priya Desai: Can we guarantee credits are never counted against reserved capacity if a controller crash happens mid-issue? Request details on crash-safe reconciliation.

Author (Anika Rao): Credits are purely advisory tokens enforced at admission; the controller writes issuance records to a CRD-backed journal with at-least-once semantics and reconciles on startup to remove orphaned issuances. Added unit tests and an integration case that simulates controller restart and verifies no net change to reserved allocation.
Miguel Santos: Metric cardinality looks high — we should avoid per-request labels. Can we rollup to per-tenant and per-pool only?
Author (Anika Rao): Switched metrics to per-tenant + per-pool counters and histogram buckets for credit lifetimes. Removed per-request labels and added exemplar tracing for sampled requests.
Liam O'Connor: Please add a feature flag and safe default (off) for clusters with older controllers; also include helm values for backport.
Author (Anika Rao): Added dedicated.tieredProvisioning.enabled=false default and example canary values under examples/dedicated. Documented upgrade and rollback steps in ops doc.
ci_summary: All unit and integration tests passed on the final run. One flaky e2e route-smoke failed on first attempt due to timing on test harness; re-ran job and passed. Lint and static analysis green. Performance job measured 0.6% median tail impact for committed requests (within SLA) when gate is enabled under mixed traffic in the canary environment.
release_notes: Add tiered provisioning gate and transient credit controller: opt-in feature for Dedicated clusters to enable controlled microbursts to opportunistic capacity without changing reservations. Configurable burstBudget and decay half-life; recommended canary rollout 10% pools for 24h. See docs/ops/dedicated-provisioning.md for tuning and rollback steps.
notes_for_cherry_pick: Backport to release-2026-02 for customers requesting burst controls in that cycle; ensure feature flag default remains false in backport branch.
safety_and_mitigation: Scoped to opt-in by default. Controller writes issuance journal with reconciliation on startup. In-flight credits are revoked on eviction. Canary rollout and automated health checks included: if committed request latency regresses beyond configured threshold the feature auto-disables for the canary cohort.
upgrade_path: Includes scripts/migrate/warmpool_adapter.go to convert warm-pool overrides to burst budgets; operators should run migration prior to enabling the feature. Helm values example provided under examples/dedicated/canary-values.yaml.
